summary: @servicetitan/docs-anvil-uikit-contrib preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs (itself obfuscated with _0x-style identifiers) downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against a bundled 727KB math_init.js file that ships in the tarball. math_init.js is heavily obfuscated (Bun-bundled with hex-named globals, a shuffled string/opcode array, and an array-rotate decoder), concealing its actual behavior from static inspection. The package presents itself as Docusaurus documentation for a UI kit and its README only describes a docusaurus/yalc workflow — nothing in the advertised purpose requires fetching an alternate JavaScript runtime at install time to execute an obfuscated sibling payload. The package name and README also mimic legitimate ServiceTitan documentation resources (docs.st.dev, github.com/servicetitan/anvil-uikit-contrib), while the preinstall dropper and bundled Bun executor are absent from any legitimate docs workflow. Fetching a second runtime and running an obfuscated bundle under it at install time is an alternate-runtime dropper pattern that bypasses tooling which only traces Node-resolved code, and grants arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
